name: Scarp Furnace
geological_features: Massive fault scarp cliffs up to 6km high
Active lava cascades down scarp faces
Magma sea in the lowland basin
specific_features: The Great Scarp -- a single cliff face 6km high and 3,000km long
description: Scarp Furnace is a volcanic world divided by the Great Scarp, a fault cliff six kilometers high and three thousand kilometers long that separates the planet's elevated crust from a lowland basin flooded with magma. Lava cascades pour over the scarp edge in curtains of molten rock, their incandescent falls visible from orbit as a line of fire drawn across the planet's surface. Mineral chimney formations grow along the scarp base where magma chemistry meets cooler rock.

The atmosphere is murderously hot and corrosive, a pressurized blanket of carbon dioxide and sulfur compounds that would destroy unshielded equipment in minutes. The magma sea in the lowland basin churns with convection currents that drive surface waves of molten rock, their crests breaking against the scarp base in slow-motion impacts. The sky above the magma sea glows a permanent, angry orange, day and night indistinguishable.

Extremophilic microbial life thrives in the mineral chimney formations along the scarp base, where chemical gradients between the magma sea and cooler groundwater create narrow habitable zones. These organisms metabolize sulfur and metal compounds, building the chimney structures as a byproduct of their biological processes. Trace amounts of exotic matter have been detected in the chimney formations, apparently concentrated by the microbial metabolic pathways -- a biological concentration process of immense scientific and economic interest.

The exotic matter traces in Scarp Furnace's biogenic chimneys have made this lethal world a priority research target. If the microbial concentration process can be understood and replicated, it could provide a biological pathway to a resource currently obtainable only through extraordinarily expensive physical processes. The challenge is operating in conditions that define the extreme end of habitable -- even by microbial standards. Every gram of data extracted from Scarp Furnace is paid for in destroyed equipment and spent shielding.
